I’ve never worked at the Institute of Acoustics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, so I can’t judge the specific environment. Last year I went along when my German boss gave a talk there. My overall impression was that the students were very capable, there were plenty of joint projects with industry and academia, and many people in acoustics circles around the world came out of there.

As for acoustics as a field, it’s on the rise right now. When I finished my master’s in 2013, the acoustics job market in China looked bleak. This year I’ve been in touch with some headhunters and companies, and demand for acoustics has clearly grown. Companies like Huawei, Tencent and Toutiao (ByteDance) are all investing in speech recognition and semantic analysis, trying to capture the voice-interaction market. From that angle, signal processing is a perfect fit. Meanwhile, NVH across the automotive industry also needs acoustics people.

Acoustics is interdisciplinary, and demand can’t compare with fields like mechanical engineering, electronics or computer science. But there aren’t many people with this expertise either, so although demand is small, hiring is often hard. If you’re interested in acoustics and have the relevant skills, finding a job shouldn’t be a problem.
